question: Should acknowledgment variation use a cheap configured strategy, a model-driven contextual choice, or remain limited to the existing static acknowledgment plus lifecycle status reactions?
rationale: The options create different public config, latency, predictability, channel-validation, and plugin-contract commitments that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Configured deterministic pool
options.body: Preserve the singular default and add an optional emoji pool with a documented deterministic selection and fallback strategy that does not invoke the model.

options.title: Model-driven contextual choice
options.body: Let the agent infer the acknowledgment from message content, accepting an additional pre-processing model or classifier step and its latency and failure implications.

options.title: Keep current reaction model
options.body: Retain one static acknowledgment and use lifecycle `statusReactions` for variation without adding another configuration or inference surface.

recommendation.title: Configured deterministic pool
recommendation.body: Preserve the singular default and add an optional emoji pool with a documented deterministic selection and fallback strategy that does not invoke the model.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed the unresolved product/API choice in the issue discussion and are the best available owner for deciding whether this new surface belongs in core.
